source_resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course: Fine-tuning LLMs
source_resources.author: Hugging Face course contributors
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Chapter 11.2: Common Template Formats; Hands-on Exercise
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Public edition checked 2026-11-01; moving pages may change
source_resources.permission_basis: External hyperlink only; no third-party prose, exercises, code or translations are imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, language-model training and the preceding chat-format lessons.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Sequenced templates, supervised fine-tuning and evaluation teaching with exercises/quizzes. LoRA method and memory claims are checked against the original paper, PEFT and the local parameter ledger, not accepted wholesale from Chapter 11.4.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Free reading; hosted exercises can require accounts, model downloads and a GPU. Chapter 11.4 overstates GPU-memory savings by implying only adapters occupy GPU memory; that sentence is not adopted.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Use the original localized explanations, exercises and checks already present in this activity; no external account or purchase is required for that fallback.

compared_candidates.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Retained for initialization and the low-rank method, not a beginner teaching sequence.
Retained for actual API and implementation defaults; reference documentation is not a complete teaching course.

source_resources.title: Stanford Alpaca: An Instruction-following LLaMA Model
source_resources.author: Rohan Taori, Ishaan Gulrajani, Tianyi Zhang, Yann Dubois, Xuechen Li, Carlos Guestrin, Percy Liang, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto
source_resources.permission_basis: Open source reference under Apache 2.0 license.
source_resources.prerequisites: LLM fine-tuning concepts, Python dictionary data structures.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Pioneering instruction fine-tuning dataset schema establishing the instruction/input/output format widely used across open source LLMs.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Public GitHub repository by Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Standard Alpaca schemas and data transformation scripts are completely specified in lesson materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wei et al. Finetuned Language Models are Zero-Shot Learners (FLAN)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pioneered academic instruction tuning across NLP benchmarks; Alpaca format provides the standardized single-turn JSON schema for consumer fine-tuning.
Commercially permissive instruction dataset; Alpaca establishes the architectural schema archetype.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: README 'Data Release' (alpaca_data.json fields instruction, input, output)

source_resources.title: OpenAI ChatML (Chat Markup Language) Specification and Guide
source_resources.author: OpenAI Documentation Team
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: openai-python tag v0.28.1, last MIT-licensed release containing chatml.md (Verified: 2026-10-31)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful reference under MIT open source documentation.
source_resources.prerequisites: Tokenizer special token concepts, conversation tree data structures.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standardized token delimiter schema (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>) separating system, user, and assistant roles to prevent prompt injection and role confusion.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: chatml.md was removed from the openai-python main branch (now Apache-2.0) in the v1 rewrite; this link is pinned to tag v0.28.1, and the page itself says it is no longer maintained.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Full ChatML delimiter specs, role headers, and token stream representations are embedded in the curriculum.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Uses Human:/Assistant: plain text delimiters; ChatML provides formal token-level demarcation with dedicated boundary tokens.
FastChat conversation template; ChatML is the universal token-delimited primitive.

activities.title: Tokenizer Special Tokens, Delimiters, and Boundary Alignment

source_resources.title: Hugging Face Transformers: Templates for Chat Models
source_resources.author: Hugging Face Documentation Team
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, Jinja2 template basics, Hugging Face PreTrainedTokenizer.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Widely adopted system for mapping list-of-dict messages into tokenized strings with tokenizer.apply_chat_template().
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete Jinja2 template implementations and boundary token unit tests are self-contained.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Configuration-driven formatting framework; Hugging Face chat templates are the direct tokenizer-level standard.
High-performance inference chat templating; HF chat templating is the training-time reference implementation.

source_resources.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
source_resources.author: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin, Kevin Stone, Peter Albert, Amjad Almahairi, et al.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines the standard LLaMA-2 instruction format ([INST] <<SYS>> ... <</SYS>> [/INST]) and analyzes token boundary alignment impact on generation stability.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The LLaMA-2 prompt structure, token boundary rules, and comparative analysis are fully worked out in curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Touvron et al. LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original foundation model paper without conversational chat tuning details; LLaMA-2 formalizes dialogue formatting.
Adopts similar [INST] formatting; LLaMA-2 provides the foundational ablation on system prompt integration.
